setting_match.planned: Rillgate Contract Hall and debt-market district
setting_match.observed: Rillgate Contract Hall, Orin's desk, Hask's stall in the debt-market district, Contract Hall, evening street outside the Hall

deviations.description: The sale date is internally inconsistent: the chapter opens with the date-line reading Sixth day and counts four days until Mira's marker sale (Tenth), but Hask says the bell rings on the fourteenth-day.

The Gray Salt run is described in beat 4 as a safe haul contract along the Gray Salt road, contradicting its earlier established description as a lethal deep-salvage mine run with iron-thread binding.

facts_contradicted.fact: Bronze rank is required to accept the contracts that pay before the tenth; unranked laborers cannot take them.
facts_contradicted.evidence: He could sign. Thumb the inked square, walk to the pay clerk, count silver before noon.
facts_contradicted.reasoning: Kael is unranked, yet the Gray Salt posting—which pays on signature before the tenth—is presented as available for him to sign.

facts_contradicted.fact: The Gray Salt Mine deep-salvage run requires iron-thread binding and has killed three men in the last six months; it is the only posting that pays before the tenth.
facts_contradicted.evidence: It was a haul contract, not a bounty. That meant the law could enforce one thing: the fee.
facts_contradicted.reasoning: The same Gray Salt posting is first established as a deep-salvage mine run with iron-thread binding and a three-death history, then in beat 4 described as a road haul contract that is safe and paper-trail-visible.

facts_contradicted.fact: Kael Rusk is unranked; his sister Mira Rusk's marker goes to sale in four days.
facts_contradicted.evidence: Date-line read Sixth day... Four days until the bell... Mira's marker went up / The bell rings the fourteenth-day. Eight sharp.
facts_contradicted.reasoning: The marker sale is four days from the Sixth day (Tenth), but Hask gives the sale date as the fourteenth-day, an eight-day gap.
